objectives: Survey the major ice-core sites + chronologies.
Reason about trapped-gas records + abrupt climate events.

slides.title: Ice-core science: drilling Earth's climate archive
slides.body:
Ice cores are the most detailed continuous record of Earth's past climate — annual layers in coastal Greenland → millennial averages in deep Antarctica. They archive temperature (via water isotopes), atmospheric composition (trapped gases), aerosols (dust, ash, sea salt, biomass), cosmogenic isotopes (¹⁰Be, ¹⁴C), and biogeochemistry (sulfate, nitrate, methanesulfonate).

**Greenland deep cores**:
- **Camp Century** (1966; US Army): first deep core to bedrock (1387 m). Dansgaard's δ¹⁸O thermometry birthplace.
- **Dye 3 + GRIP + GISP2** (1980s-1993): central + south Greenland. ~110 kyr record. Discovered **Dansgaard-Oeschger events** (abrupt warmings ~20 cycles in last glacial).
- **NorthGRIP (NGRIP)** + **NEEM** + **EastGRIP**: 2000s-present. Extended record to ~123 kyr (Eemian); informed by Willi Dansgaard, Hans Oeschger, Sigfús Johnsen, Bo Vinther, Jørgen Peder Steffensen.

**Antarctic deep cores**:
- **Byrd Station** (1968; ~2164 m): pioneering WAIS core.
- **Vostok** (Russian-French; 1990s-1998): central East Antarctica; 3623 m; ~420 kyr record. Petit + Jouzel + Lorius 1999 Nature paper on Vostok was a landmark in paleoclimate, definitively linking CO₂ + CH₄ to glacial-interglacial cycles.
- **EPICA Dome C** (European Project for Ice Coring in Antarctica; 2004): 3270 m; **~800 kyr record** — the longest continuous ice-core record to date. EPICA Community 2004 + 2006 Nature papers. Eight glacial cycles. **Claude Lorius, Jean Jouzel, Jean-Robert Petit, Dominique Raynaud, Eric Wolff, Hubertus Fischer** key contributors.
- **EPICA Dronning Maud Land (EDML)**: bipolar correlation.
- **WAIS Divide (WDC)** (2011): 3405 m; high-resolution Holocene + last glacial; first high-accumulation Antarctic record at annual resolution for the last ~30 kyr.
- **Beyond EPICA-Oldest Ice** (in progress): targeting **>1.5 Myr** to span the Mid-Pleistocene Transition (when ice ages shifted from ~41 kyr to ~100 kyr period). EU consortium + Italian-led drilling at Little Dome C.
- **Allan Hills blue-ice** (US): discontinuous record but extends to **>2.7 Myr** by analyzing 'old ice' patches.

**Drilling technology**: thermal drills (Russian Vostok) — efficient at depth but contamination risk. Electromechanical with drilling fluid (Estisol, n-butyl acetate) — modern standard. Replicate coring for redundancy. Field campaigns 3-5 austral summers; ~$30-60M per deep core.

**Chronology**: layer counting (annual layers visible in dust, isotopes, conductivity) in upper few km; ice-flow modeling + volcanic-tephra tie-points + orbital tuning at depth. Greenland Ice Core Chronology (GICC05; Rasmussen, Vinther, Steffensen) is now the reference.

slides.title: Isotope paleothermometry: δ¹⁸O + δD + Dansgaard's calibration
slides.body:
**Water isotopes** record temperature because heavier isotopes (H₂¹⁸O, HDO vs H₂¹⁶O) fractionate during evaporation + condensation. Rayleigh distillation: as an air mass cools en route from source to ice sheet, condensation preferentially removes heavy isotopes; the remaining vapor (and the snow that falls from it) becomes progressively isotopically lighter.

**δ notation**: δ¹⁸O = ((¹⁸O/¹⁶O)_sample / (¹⁸O/¹⁶O)_VSMOW − 1) × 1000 ‰ (per mil). VSMOW = Vienna Standard Mean Ocean Water (≈0 ‰). Glacial-age Greenland ice: δ¹⁸O ≈ −42 ‰; modern values ≈ −35 ‰. Antarctic interior: δ¹⁸O ≈ −55 ‰.

**Dansgaard's empirical calibration** (Dansgaard 1964 Tellus + 1969 Science):
  δ¹⁸O ≈ 0.69 × T_avg − 13.6 ‰ (modern coastal Greenland)
→ ~0.7 ‰ per °C (typical mid-high latitude).

For Antarctic interior (lower temperatures, longer Rayleigh path): ~0.8 ‰/°C.

**Deuterium δD**: scales with δ¹⁸O via the **Meteoric Water Line** (δD ≈ 8 × δ¹⁸O + 10, Craig 1961). Deviation gives **deuterium excess (d-excess = δD − 8 δ¹⁸O)** — a proxy for moisture-source ocean conditions (SST, humidity).

**Calibration issues**:
- Modern spatial slope (δ-T from coring multiple sites) ≠ temporal slope (δ-T at one site over time).
- **Borehole-thermometry** (downhole T profiles + heat-flow modeling) gives independent T calibration (Cuffey + Clow 1995; Dahl-Jensen 1998) — typical Last Glacial Maximum (LGM) cooling ~20-25 °C in central Greenland (more than the spatial slope would suggest).
- **Noble-gas thermometry** (Severinghaus; Buizert; Caillon) from firn-air N₂/Ar/Xe isotope fractionation gives precise glacial-Holocene T differences.

**Milankovitch + orbital forcing** (Milutin Milanković 1920s; Hays + Imbrie + Shackleton 1976 Science):
- Eccentricity (~100 kyr): orbital ellipticity → small annual-mean insolation modulation.
- Obliquity (~41 kyr): axial tilt → seasonal contrast at high latitudes.
- Precession (~21 kyr): timing of perihelion → hemispheric seasonal asymmetry.
- Drove the ~100 kyr glacial cycles of the late Quaternary; CO₂ + ice-albedo feedbacks amplified.

**Glacial-interglacial cycles** (last 800 kyr from EPICA):
- ~100 kyr periodicity.
- Temperature swings ~5-6 °C globally; ~10-12 °C polar; ~3-5 °C tropical.
- CO₂ varies between ~180 ppm (glacial) + ~280 ppm (interglacial pre-industrial). Modern: 420 ppm (2024) — higher than any time in the 800 kyr record.
- Methane (CH₄): glacial ~350 ppb / interglacial ~700 ppb / modern ~1930 ppb.
- Asymmetry: slow cooling into glacial (~80 kyr); rapid deglaciation (~10 kyr).
- **Mid-Pleistocene Transition (MPT, ~1.2-0.7 Ma)**: dominant period shifted ~41 kyr → ~100 kyr. Mechanism debated (CO₂, ice-sheet thickness, regolith); 'oldest-ice' efforts to constrain it.

slides.title: Trapped gases, CO₂, methane + abrupt climate events
slides.body:
When snow compacts to firn + finally to ice (close-off ~830 kg/m³ at ~50-100 m depth), atmospheric air is **sealed in bubbles** — a direct sample of the past atmosphere. This is the most direct paleoclimate measurement; precision now ~1 ppm CO₂ over 800 kyr (EPICA, Vostok, WAIS Divide; Lüthi 2008 Nature).

**Gas-age vs ice-age offset**: gas trapped is younger than the ice surrounding it (~10-300 yr younger in high-accumulation sites, ~2000-7000 yr in low-accumulation EPICA). Critical for inferring lead-lag relationships between CO₂ + temperature.

**CO₂ record (Lüthi 2008; Bereiter 2015; Higgins 2015)**:
- 180 ppm (glacial max) → 280 ppm (interglacial) over 800 kyr.
- Lagged temperature by ~600 ± 400 yr at glacial *terminations* (Caillon 2003; Parrenin 2013) — but during glaciations CO₂ leads. CO₂ amplifies but does not initiate Milankovitch-paced cycles.
- Modern CO₂ ~420 ppm: higher than any time in the 800 kyr record; likely higher than any time in 2-3 Myr (Pliocene); rate of increase ~100× faster than any natural deglaciation.

**Methane (CH₄)**:
- Northern Hemisphere wetlands + boreal source dominate; rapid response to climate.
- Glacial-interglacial 350 → 700 ppb. Modern ~1930 ppb (anthropogenic agriculture + fossil + thaw).
- **Bipolar phasing**: methane is well-mixed globally → use to synchronize Greenland + Antarctic timescales (Blunier; WAIS Divide Project 2015).

**Abrupt climate events** in Greenland cores:
- **Dansgaard-Oeschger (D-O) events** (Dansgaard 1969; Oeschger 1984; Bond 1993): ~25 abrupt warmings during last glacial (115-15 kyr ago), each 5-15 °C in Greenland over decades; ~2-3 kyr stable warm interstadial; then gradual cooling + abrupt return to cold stadial. Pattern: 'Bond cycles' grouped in ~5 D-O + Heinrich event.
- **Heinrich events**: ice-rafted debris layers in N Atlantic sediment cores; massive iceberg discharges from Laurentide Ice Sheet (Hudson Strait). Linked to D-O cold stadials.
- **Younger Dryas** (12.9-11.7 kyr BP): abrupt return to glacial conditions during last deglaciation. Triggered (most likely) by freshwater pulse from Lake Agassiz / Laurentide meltwater drainage into N Atlantic, shutting down AMOC. **Wally Broecker** (Lamont-Doherty) was the leading articulator of this AMOC-Younger-Dryas connection (1980s-2000s; many Nature + Science papers).
- **8.2 ka event** (8.2 kyr BP): ~2-3 °C Greenland cooling for ~160 yr; triggered by Lake Agassiz catastrophic drainage; affected N Atlantic + monsoon + early agriculture societies.
- **Bipolar see-saw** (Stocker + Johnsen 2003): when AMOC weakens, N hemisphere cools while S hemisphere warms (heat redistribution); WAIS Divide + EPICA records confirm Antarctic warming during Greenland stadials.

**Dust records**:
- Glacial periods 10-100× higher dust flux to ice cores; sources Patagonia (Antarctica) + Asian deserts (Gobi for Greenland).
- Dust is biogeochemically active — iron fertilizes Southern Ocean productivity → CO₂ drawdown (Martin's 'iron hypothesis'; Latimer + Filippelli 2002).

**Volcanic record** (sulfate spikes): Toba 74 ka, Tambora 1815, Krakatoa 1883, Pinatubo 1991 all visible in cores. Used for synchronization.

**Connection to Pääbo + ancient DNA**: ice + permafrost preserve biomolecules. Svante Pääbo's Neanderthal + Denisovan genomes (Nobel 2022) plus environmental aDNA from permafrost + ice (Willerslev) extend climate-biology coupling. Ice cores + sediments + cave deposits + ancient DNA together reconstruct Pleistocene Earth-biosphere co-evolution.

**Frontier**:
- **Beyond EPICA Oldest Ice (2024+)**: aiming >1.5 Myr to resolve MPT.
- **Continuous-flow analysis (CFA)**: real-time chemistry, methane, particulate measurement during melting. 1-cm resolution over 800 kyr feasible.
- **Climate models calibrated to abrupt events**: testing AMOC + ice-sheet models against D-O + Younger Dryas + 8.2 ka.

question.question: Estimate paleotemperature from a Greenland ice-core δ¹⁸O measurement
question.goal: An NGRIP ice-core sample shows δ¹⁸O = −42 ‰. Modern site δ¹⁸O = −35 ‰; modern annual T ≈ −31 °C. Use Dansgaard's slope dδ¹⁸O/dT ≈ 0.7 ‰/°C to estimate the paleotemperature + interpret.

steps.reveal: Δδ¹⁸O = −42 − (−35) = −7 ‰. Sample isotopically depleted relative to modern → colder.
ΔT = Δδ¹⁸O / (dδ/dT) = −7 ‰ / 0.7 ‰/°C = −10 °C. Sample period ~10 °C cooler than today.

T_paleo ≈ −31 + (−10) = −41 °C. Consistent with Last Glacial Maximum (LGM, ~21 kyr BP) Greenland conditions — borehole thermometry (Cuffey + Clow) actually suggests LGM Greenland ~25 °C colder, so the Dansgaard slope under-estimates glacial cooling (temporal vs spatial slope issue). Modern reconstructions combine δ¹⁸O + borehole + noble-gas thermometry.

acceptedAnswers: different mechanisms; need borehole or noble-gas calibration
Dansgaard slope is from modern site network, not from one site over time

steps.reveal: The 0.7 ‰/°C 'Dansgaard slope' is derived from a *modern spatial gradient* across Greenland sites at different elevations + latitudes. The *temporal* slope at one site through time differs (due to seasonality changes, moisture-source shifts, elevation changes, ice-sheet topography evolution). Borehole thermometry (Cuffey + Clow 1995; Dahl-Jensen 1998) + noble-gas thermometry (Severinghaus; Buizert) gave temporal slope ~0.3-0.5 ‰/°C, implying LGM cooling 22-25 °C (greater than Dansgaard linear). This insight reshaped paleoclimate reconstructions + climate-sensitivity inferences.

question.question: Why does the 800-kyr EPICA Dome C ice-core record show CO₂ varying between ~180 + 280 ppm, while modern CO₂ is ~420 ppm?
options: Throughout the last 800 kyr (and likely the last 2-3 Myr) atmospheric CO₂ was paced by Milankovitch orbital forcing + amplified by carbon-cycle feedbacks (ocean solubility + Southern Ocean ventilation + iron fertilization + biosphere). Pre-industrial Holocene equilibrium ~280 ppm (CO₂ trapped in EPICA + Vostok + Law Dome + Taylor Dome firn-ice transition); glacial minima ~180 ppm (LGM). Anthropogenic fossil-fuel + land-use emissions ~600 Gt C since 1750 raised CO₂ to ~420 ppm (2024) — ~50% above the natural Quaternary maximum. Rate of rise (~2.5 ppm/yr current) is ~100× faster than any natural transition observed in the ice-core record. This makes modern CO₂ both unprecedented in concentration + in rate over the last 2-3 Myr (ice-core 800 kyr + boron-isotope, alkenone, leaf-stomata proxies for older periods). IPCC AR6 unequivocal attribution to anthropogenic forcing.
question.explanation: EPICA Dome C + Vostok: natural Quaternary CO₂ between 180 ppm (glacial) + 280 ppm (interglacial), paced by Milankovitch + amplified by carbon-cycle feedbacks. Modern 420 ppm is ~50% above the natural maximum; rate of increase ~100× faster than any natural transition. Older proxies (boron isotopes, alkenones) confirm 420 ppm unprecedented over 2-3 Myr. AR6 confidently attributes to anthropogenic emissions.

hints: How does the modern rate compare?
slides.workedSolution: Natural Quaternary CO₂ varied 180-280 ppm (glacial-interglacial). Modern 420 ppm ~50% above natural max + ~100× faster rate of change. Older proxies suggest 420 ppm unprecedented in 2-3 Myr. Anthropogenic, AR6 unequivocal.

question.question: An anomalous methane spike in a new core
question.prompt: Your group measures a previously-unreported 200-ppb CH₄ spike at ~6.5 ka BP in a new ice core, lasting ~100 yr. How would you (a) check it's not contamination or analytical artifact, (b) confirm by cross-referencing other cores, and (c) attribute to a likely natural source (wetland, fire, hydrate, biomass)?

question.question: Glacial-interglacial CO₂ ranges 180-280 ppm. Modern 420 ppm. By what % above the pre-industrial maximum is modern CO₂?

question.prompt: In ≤120 words, explain why ice cores are the 'gold standard' paleoclimate archive + which key discoveries they made possible.
question.rubric: Mentions: ice cores combine direct atmosphere samples (trapped gas bubbles → CO₂, CH₄, isotopes, noble gases) with proxies (water isotopes δ¹⁸O δD for T; dust + sea salt + sulfate + ¹⁰Be for circulation + solar + volcanism) at sub-annual to annual resolution for the recent past, decadal for the deep past. Continuous, high-fidelity, in-situ. Key discoveries: (1) Dansgaard 1964 + 1969 — sequence-temperature calibration + first abrupt-event detection; (2) Vostok + EPICA (Lorius + Jouzel + Petit) — direct demonstration that CO₂ + CH₄ + T co-vary across 8 glacial cycles, supporting climate-sensitivity inferences; (3) Dansgaard-Oeschger events + Younger Dryas (Broecker AMOC connection); (4) 8.2 ka event + ENSO + monsoon variability; (5) modern CO₂ unprecedented in 800 kyr (likely 2-3 Myr). Underpins IPCC AR6 attribution + climate-sensitivity estimates. Frontier: Beyond-EPICA Oldest Ice + sub-annual chemistry.
